paragraphs: Begin by collecting materials and reviewing drawings and the work briefing. Lift and position components, tack-weld them in place, then complete root and cover passes. Perform overhead welds inside a hot tank at midday. Conduct pressure tests and check for leaks in the afternoon, finishing only after the gauge remains stable. A safety officer monitors hazardous work throughout.

paragraphs: A score of 3/10 places this occupation in the relatively low AI-exposure range. Core assembly and welding depend on hands-on skill, while only peripheral tasks become digital.

Relatively low exposure is not a reason to stand still. Layout and material cutting are being replaced, not welding and assembly. Technicians who handle difficult welds and manage safety remain scarce, while entry-level workers limited to simple joining face the greatest risk.

This trade suits people who combine steady hands, physical strength, and safety discipline. In high-temperature, high-pressure steel environments, the work must be both high quality and safe.

The hardest part of this trade is the weight. Components can weigh several tons, spaces are cramped, and a single weld can require hours in an awkward position. It suits people with steady hands who accept dirty work at height and in confined spaces.
Prefers hands-on practical work within clear rules (Realistic R + Conventional C + Investigative I).
If you are precise with your hands, confident in your judgment, and able to work safely in hazardous environments, boilermaking is a well-paid skilled trade with persistent shortages.

subject.summary: Boilermakers build the frames of high-pressure vessels. The tanks and pipes that withstand high temperatures and pressures in power plants, refineries, and ships ultimately depend on their hands for assembly and secure welding.
